subject: gov.policy
name: 'Fully digitalised e-government by 2030' target
milestone: President Herminie reaffirmed the target while receiving Malta's first High Commissioner's credentials, exploring bilateral technical cooperation
position_end: Restated 4 Aug 2026; route named is bilateral technical assistance from Malta, no domestic implementation programme named

subject: gov.policy
name: Commission of Inquiry into the border management service agreement
milestone: Opened 2 September 2026; former ministers testified
position_end: A commission of inquiry into the border management service agreement between the state and its border-security supplier opened at the Palais de Justice on 2 September 2026. The supplier's system is used by the immigration and civil status department as part of digital border control, including the electronic travel authorisation issued to visitors. The commission was established by the president after an announcement in the State of the Nation Address, framed as a commitment to transparency and accountability in public administration; it has heard testimony from two former ministers on how the state initially explored established international providers before the supplier entered the picture
note: both accounts are paywalled beyond their opening passages, so the commission's terms of reference, its members and the substance of the testimony are not established here

subject: gov.policy
name: Fixed Broadband Wireless Access policy for the 2.4 and 5.8 GHz bands
milestone: Revised policy issued by the regulator, superseding the 2004 policy
position_end: The regulator's revised licence-exemption and spectrum policy for fixed broadband wireless access is the closest thing the base holds to a broadband instrument; no standalone national broadband strategy is held

subject: gov.policy
name: Multidimensional Vulnerability Index (MVI) operationalisation
milestone: Cabinet approved national measures naming enhanced data and institutional capacity and alignment of planning/budgeting frameworks as the instruments
position_end: Cabinet decision only; no implementation detail, budget or timeline on record

subject: gov.policy
name: National Development Strategy 2024-2028
milestone: Published for 2024-2028, succeeding NDS 2019-2023
position_end: The current national strategy, continuing NDS 2019-2023, puts "A Modern Public Service" as Priority Area 1, emphasising technology and streamlined processes
note: the held capture is an excerpt of a 142-page document; no costed digital annex or delivery report against it is on file

subject: gov.policy
name: National ICT Policy
milestone: Adopted 2007; no revision on record
position_end: The National ICT Policy is the standing whole-of-government ICT instrument, covering ICT infrastructure, the legal and regulatory framework, human resources, industry and government. Nineteen years on, no successor, revision or evaluation of it is held
note: the document carries no date on its face; 2007 is taken from a third-party policy portal

subject: gov.policy
name: National Institute for Science, Technology and Innovation (the body)
milestone: Reinstated with its Secretariat under the Office of the Vice-President, described 2026-08-10
position_start: Closed shortly after the 2020 election and its functions folded into a ministry division, which the Secretary of State describes as costing the institution its operational independence and much of its technical staff
position_end: Reinstated as the implementation arm for science, technology and innovation policy, its Secretariat sitting under the Office of the Vice-President under a Secretary of State, with a stated near-term focus on technological innovation in government procedures and accelerating the digitalisation of public-service delivery
note: the NISTI Act 2025 is recorded separately and no commencement notice for it is on record; the body is described as functioning without one being cited

subject: gov.policy
name: Open Government Partnership National Action Plan 2023-2025
milestone: Cabinet-approved 13 December 2023
position_end: The second national action plan carries Commitment 3, Digital Transformation and Connecting People, aiming to raise general-population IT literacy through public education, mobile training and district computer rooms; its own background section records that the citizen e-engagement feedback portal commitment has not begun

subject: gov.policy
name: Seychelles Spatial Data Sharing Policy 2020
milestone: Adopted by the lands ministry, 2020
position_end: A sectoral spatial-data sharing policy adopting UN-GGIM principles and OGC and ISO interoperability standards across ministries, and providing for distributed data-centre hosting. It is the nearest instrument the base holds to either a cloud strategy or a data interoperability framework, and it is not a whole-of-government one

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Act 2018 (ATIA) reform
milestone: InfoCom whitepaper recommends a centralised Access-to-Information Unit, aligning s.33(4) with the DPA 2023, open-reuse licensing; AG drafting targeted end-2025
position_end: Whitepaper published, drafting targeted end-2025; no Bill text or introduction date on record
note: Same InfoCom body holds both the ATI and DPA mandates

subject: gov.legislate
name: Civil Status (Amendment) Act 2021
milestone: Act 45 of 2021, gazetted 4 November 2021
position_end: The Act inserts section 18A into the Civil Status Act, a statutory duty to reproduce every disused register — births, stillbirths, deaths, marriages, divorces, adoptions and name changes — into digital format and preserve them indefinitely, and section 107A enabling electronic submissions and signatures
note: no completion figure, digitisation programme report or count of registers converted under section 18A is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Communications Act 2023
milestone: Act 3 of 2023, assented 13 April 2023
position_end: The consolidated communications statute establishes the Seychelles Communications Regulatory Authority and runs to licensing, fair competition, consumer protection, interconnection, access, tariffs, the processing of personal data and, at Part XII, universal access and universal service policy, obligations and a fund
note: the held capture is an excerpt; no disbursement, designated provider or coverage target under the universal service fund is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes and Other Related Crimes Act 2021 and its 2025 amendment
milestone: Amendment Act 23 of 2025 assented 22 December 2025
position_end: The 2021 Act created the first standalone cybercrime offences regime, repealing the Computer Misuse Act, and commenced 1 February 2022. The 2025 amendment, passed 15 December and assented 22 December 2025, widens the offence definitions, defines subscriber information as identity, address and billing or service details, and adds search and interception powers
note: no prosecution, caseload or enforcement figure under either instrument is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Transactions Act 2001
milestone: Act 8 of 2001; consolidated text current to 29 March 2018
position_end: The founding electronic-commerce statute, giving legal recognition to electronic records, digital signatures and electronic dealings with public authorities
note: S.I. 12 of 2024 amended the exclusions Schedule and is not applied to the consolidated text held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Financial Consumer Protection Act 2022
milestone: Act 6 of 2022, assented 14 April 2022
position_end: Seychelles' first financial-consumer-protection statute, whose Schedule Part A expressly covers payment service providers and the operators of payment, clearing and settlement systems under the National Payment System Act
note: no complaints statistic, redress figure or supervisory action under the Act is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Assembly Administration Act 2026
milestone: Act 8 of 2026, gazetted 15 June 2026
position_end: The Act creates an autonomous Parliamentary Service with, at section 16, a dedicated Office of Information Technology, Cybersecurity and Data Security, a Parliamentary Budget Office, and financial-autonomy provisions putting parliamentary appropriations and retained underspend under the Commission

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Bureau of Statistics Act 2010
milestone: Assented 9 July 2010, repealing the 2005 Act
position_end: The founding statute for the National Bureau of Statistics and the national statistical system. The African Union's 2025 peer review records the Bureau's professional independence and recommends a new Statistics Bill
note: no standalone national data-governance policy is held; this statute is the closest institutional instrument to one

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Identity Cards Act as amended by the Miscellaneous Amendments Act 2023
milestone: Part 13 of Act 22 of 2023
position_end: Part 13 of the 2023 omnibus Act amends the National Identity Cards Act on the national identity number requirement, cards for non-resident citizens and information-disclosure rules; it does not itself create the SeyID digital credential. The 2025 cybercrimes amendment separately defines subscriber information for evidential purposes
note: no statute names or governs the SeyID credential itself, which rests on administrative practice

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payment System Act 2014 and its licensing regulations
milestone: Licensing and Authorisation (Amendment) Regulations made 15 December 2025
position_end: The founding payment-system statute, Act 14 of 2014, commenced 18 August 2014 and has been amended by the 2022 electronic money regulations and a 2023 amendment Act. The December 2025 amendment to the licensing and authorisation regulations makes safe, reliable IT systems and adequate interfaces for straight-through processing a licensing condition for payment, clearing and settlement operators
note: the statute's operative text is held only as a citation and history record; the reader-facing PDF could not be resolved

subject: gov.legislate
name: NISTI Act 2025 (National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation)
milestone: Act 24 of 2025 assented; establishes NISTI as a body corporate with an AI-strategy mandate, a Science Academy, an open-access scientific-data repository, incubation centres
position_end: Assented 22 Dec 2025; commences on a date the Minister appoints — no commencement date on record

subject: gov.legislate
name: Seychelles Broadcasting Corporation Act 2026
milestone: Assented 9 July 2026, gazetted 13 July 2026
position_end: The Act repeals the 2011 statute and requires the Corporation to develop and periodically review a policy on the use of artificial intelligence in content creation, curation and broadcast operations. It is the only statutory artificial-intelligence obligation the base holds for Seychelles
note: the policy the Act requires is not itself held, and no general AI statute or regulation exists

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Act 2023 (Act 24 of 2023)
milestone: s.56(1)'s 18-month transition (from the 22 Dec 2023 commencement) elapsed; controllers/processors now subject to the Act in full
position_start: Transition already elapsed and Act binding in full at the 2025-08 baseline
position_end: Unchanged; no source reports any investigation, audit, fine or guidance issued by the Information Commission since
sources: 2023-12-22-seychelles-data-protection-act-2023-act-24|2024-03-25 Data Protection Law Now In Force In Seychelles|2024-06-04 Review of Seychelles DPA|2026-03-12 Africa’s Data Protection Reforms A Continental Perspective on the Drivers of Change in Legal Frameworks
note: FPF (2026-03-12) adds that the Act expressly recognises participation in the Global CBPR System

subject: gov.protect
name: Information Commission (data-protection authority)
milestone: Second information-officer induction session of 2026 held
position_end: Designated authority since December 2023, with an enforcement-capacity gap documented in November 2025 and no audit, investigation or fine against any controller reported to date. It runs two induction sessions a year for information officers newly appointed by public bodies and held the second of 2026 on 31 August, led by its chief executive and a senior information analyst
note: induction of the officers public bodies must appoint is the commission's visible activity; the enforcement half of its mandate still shows no case, and no count of officers inducted or bodies covered is published

subject: gov.regional
name: AfCFTA Protocol on Digital Trade obligations
milestone: Assembly decision of 14-15 February 2026 urging operationalisation
position_end: The African Union Assembly, at its 39th Ordinary Session, urged AfCFTA State Parties to operationalise their digital public infrastructure commitments on cross-border data protection and transfers under the Protocol on Digital Trade
note: nothing records what Seychelles has done under the Protocol; the decision is a continental instruction, not a national step

subject: gov.regional
name: AUDA-NEPAD Programme for African Developing Island Economies
milestone: AUDA-NEPAD launched the programme at the AU's STC Ministerial Segment (Abidjan), covering seven island states including Seychelles; 2026–2031 roadmap, six pillars including digital transformation
position_end: Programme launched, communique adopted; partners include Korea, AfDB, RECs, the Indian Ocean Commission

subject: gov.regional
name: SADC Treaty and its Protocol mechanism
milestone: Founding High Contracting Party; 2025 consolidated text published August 2026
position_end: Seychelles is named among the founding High Contracting Parties in the Treaty's preamble; the consolidated 2025 edition sets out SADC's institutions, its areas of co-operation and the Protocol mechanism through which regional legal harmonisation is done
note: no Seychelles ratification instrument for any specific digital or data protocol is held

subject: gov.standards
name: Government-wide interoperability standards (DICT Policy, Standards and Research Section)
milestone: Standing mandate of the department
position_end: The department's own statement of its Policy, Standards and Research Section puts adopted technical standards for the seamless interoperability of e-government services, and the integration of every e-government application and database through established software and database standards, within its mandate
note: the standards themselves are not published, so what is held is the mandate rather than the framework

subject: gov.standards
name: Seychelles Bureau of Standards
milestone: Board of eight appointed for three years from 1 August 2025
position_end: The Bureau is constituted under Act 2 of 2014, commenced 16 June 2014 and amended in 2016 and 2021, whose 36 sections set the Board, the standards-making procedure, offences and penalties. A new eight-member Board was appointed for three years from 1 August 2025, and the regional accreditation service's register shows the Bureau's mass-calibration capability approved on 15 September 2025 and valid to 14 September 2030
note: no count of national standards adopted, nor an annual report of the Bureau, is held

subject: gov.discourse
name: Appointment and dismissal power over the SBC board
milestone: Seychelles Broadcasting Corporation Act amended by Parliament, June 2026
position_start: Vested in the independent Constitutional Appointments Authority
position_end: Greater powers over the appointment and dismissal of the public broadcaster's board transferred to the President by a June 2026 amendment to the SBC Act
note: the base holds no primary text of the amendment; it is reported in Afrobarometer's dispatch, citing Broadcast Media Africa and the International Press Institute

subject: gov.discourse
name: Perceived media freedom
milestone: Afrobarometer round fielded 2025, dispatch published 2026-08-11
position_start: 51% said the media was somewhat or completely free (2022)
position_end: 45% say the media is somewhat or completely free and 52% say it is not very or not at all free (2025 survey), against 78% who want the media to investigate government mistakes and corruption and 85% who back the right to publish without government interference
note: a perception measure, not an assessment of the media's legal position; Reporters Without Borders placed Seychelles 35th globally in 2026, up ten places

subject: gov.discourse
name: Published Cabinet business record
milestone: Record of the meeting of 26 August 2026 published
position_end: The State House continues to publish a record of each Cabinet meeting; the record of 26 August 2026 is held
note: A standing transparency practice, which is why it is a row rather than an event.

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic-state digital-transformation budget line
status: Implemented, an annual departmental line rather than a dedicated fund
milestone: Appropriation Act 2026 assented 23 March 2026
position_end: The 2026 Consolidated Fund appropriation authorises R11,842,682,521 of total expenditure and appropriates R93.813 million to the Department of Information Communications Technology — an annual departmental allocation, not a dedicated multi-year digital-transformation fund. The National Assembly Administration Act 2026 separately creates an autonomous Parliamentary Service carrying its own Office of Information Technology, Cybersecurity and Data Security and its own budget
note: the appropriation gives one departmental figure and no programme breakdown, so what is spent on digital transformation across the rest of government is not established

subject: finance.mou
name: Mauritius Telecom–Eboo cross-border payments
milestone: Mauritius Telecom CEO Veemal Gungadin announced cross-border payment capabilities between Mauritius and Seychelles, in partnership with Eboo, a Seychelles fintech
position_end: Announced at the AllMyT Summit as the first of a planned series of Indian Ocean regional payment announcements; no operational detail, launch date or terms given
note: Single paragraph in an otherwise Mauritius-focused keynote

subject: finance.new
name: Hustle Fund et al. → Fusepay pre-seed
milestone: US$350,000 pre-seed: Hustle Fund, Everywhere Ventures, First Check Ventures, Startup Istanbul, Ryan Nesbitt (angel)
position_end: Round closed; platform launched Nov 2025, Fuse360 AI layer added Jul 2026
note: Same underlying article held twice under two slugs — see byproducts note

subject: finance.new
name: TDB → CWS debt refinancing and digital-transformation facility
milestone: US$50m package refinancing US$48.1m of the 2019 debt; TDB acquired ~2.9% CWS equity (Dec 2022); CWS listed on the MERJ Exchange (Sep 2022); TDB co-arranged a SCR 168m (~US$12.5m) local-currency bond (Feb 2024)
position_end: Unchanged; supports CWS's eBill, self-care and online-registration platforms, and Nebula Fintech exploration

subject: finance.new
name: TDB → CWS Investment Ltd acquisition financing
milestone: TDB arranged US$70m syndicated acquisition financing (US$50m own book) for CWS Investment Ltd to acquire Cable & Wireless Seychelles from Liberty Latin America
position_end: Unchanged; refinanced in 2022

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank Seychelles Social Protection PforR (PAD3541)
milestone: US$30m Program-for-Results; digital element is the social-protection registry/MIS
position_end: Unchanged; no completion or closure report on record
sources: 2021-03-03 PAD - Seychelles Strengthening Quality of the Social Protection System PforR (PAD3541)
note: Same underlying World Bank document held twice under two slugs — see byproducts note

subject: infra.connect
name: Airtel Seychelles 5G network
milestone: Commercial 5G launch, Airtel House; SBC content partnership announced alongside
position_start: No 5G service; network being relocated/virtualised into new datacentre (2025-08)
position_end: Commercial 5G live, second operator after CWS
note: Plan/pricing detail is paywalled, not held

subject: infra.connect
name: Cable & Wireless Seychelles 4G/5G network
milestone: CWS launched 5G with Huawei as vendor
position_start: 5G live since Jul 2020, unchanged at 2025-08 baseline
position_end: Unchanged; now running alongside Airtel's newer 5G network

subject: infra.connect
name: Cable and Wireless national fibre broadband network
milestone: Nationwide 50G-PON upgrade, April 2026
position_end: The incumbent raised entry-level unlimited plans to a minimum of 60 Mbps and capped plans to a minimum 30 GB across its fibre network, on newly deployed 50G-PON technology, at no extra cost. The competing operator had launched unlimited home broadband from R999 for 10 Mbps in September 2025, with a R200 booster to 200 Mbps
note: neither operator publishes subscriber numbers or coverage by district, and the fibre upgrade is announced by the operator rather than verified by the regulator

subject: infra.connect
name: Hytera–CWS emergency-communications MoU
milestone: MoU signed at MWC 2025 for a resilient PoC/MCX emergency-comms core integrating with CWS 4G/5G
position_start: MoU signed, no build reported (2025-08 baseline)
position_end: Unchanged — no build, commissioning date or further progress on record
note: No update on this MoU in over 17 months

subject: infra.connect
name: International internet bandwidth
milestone: Q1 2026 regulator statistics
position_end: 308,074 Mbps at 31 March 2026 — 154,023 uplink and 154,051 downlink — unchanged on the quarter, against 17,870 Mbps at the start of the regulator's published series in March 2020

subject: infra.connect
name: International submarine backbone (SEAS and PEACE)
milestone: PEACE cable in service 16 November 2022
position_end: The SEAS cable, commissioned over a decade earlier, was the sole international submarine backbone until the PEACE cable came into service on 16 November 2022, ending reliance on a single link and adding resilience and capacity
note: no capacity, utilisation or outage figure for either cable is published

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet usage
milestone: World Bank and ITU series, 2024 value
position_start: 79.3 per cent of the population in 2020
position_end: 87.8 per cent of the population using the internet in 2024, against 79.3 per cent in 2020; a commercial tracker puts 117,000 users and 87.4 per cent penetration at October 2025, leaving an estimated 16,800 people, 12.6 per cent, offline
note: the two series are close but differently constructed, and no national survey of who is offline and why is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Prepaid mobile and e-SIM regulations
milestone: Cabinet approval, 18 March 2026
position_end: Cabinet approved amendments to the 2009 and 2021 broadcasting and telecommunications regulations governing prepaid mobile services: e-SIM sales through digital platforms, mandatory annual operator audits and a 21-day limit on tourist and non-resident SIMs
note: the amendments modernise compliance rather than tariffs, and no enacted instrument is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Seychelles Internet Exchange Point
milestone: Launched under the African Union AXIS project, February 2015
position_end: Launched under the African Union's AXIS project with the Department of ICT, to keep intra-country internet traffic inside the country
note: eleven years on, no peering count, traffic figure or operating statement for the exchange point is held, and nothing more current than the launch announcement was found

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink Seychelles (satellite ISP)
milestone: Soft-launch briefing, State House, VP Pillay + SCRA confirm authorisation
position_end: Live nationally, subscriptions open online, several users already active (2026-07-21/22); 28th of 54 African markets on sale
note: Cabinet approved the ISP licence 18 Feb 2026; incorporated locally and in final licensing by May 2026

subject: infra.store
name: Airtel Seychelles data centre (Ericsson turnkey project)
milestone: Ericsson awarded turnkey project to relocate/modernise Airtel's network into a new datacentre, hybrid network cloud
position_end: A Tier III facility at Perseverance with redundant power and cooling, offered for colocation and customer disaster recovery with 24-hour monitoring; it is the only off-site backup capacity the base records inside the country
note: Only inferred still-operating via the 2026 5G launch it enabled

subject: infra.store
name: Bon Espoir Tier IV data centre (Cable and Wireless)
milestone: Tier IV design certification issued 4 September 2025; opened March 2026
position_end: The country's first Tier IV certified data centre, at Anse Boileau, positioned by its operator as keeping government services and financial institutions onshore rather than on overseas facilities. The certifying body's own record names Cable and Wireless (Seychelles) Limited as client and dates the Tier IV construction and design award to 4 September 2025, valid to 2027
note: no floor area, rack count, power capacity or customer list is published, and the operating announcement is the operator’s own

subject: infra.energy
name: National policy linking digital infrastructure to energy supply
position_end: Not held
note: No source on file

subject: infra.energy
name: Public Utilities Corporation electricity supply
milestone: Operator annual report for 2024
position_start: 99.5 per cent coverage and 45,364 customers in 2023
position_end: The utility reports 99.5 per cent electricity coverage in both 2023 and 2024, 45,364 customers and 1,279 employees, generating assets at Roche Caiman 77.5 MW, New Port 28.75 MW, Baie Ste Anne 15.39 MW and La Digue 2.46 MW, a South Mahe 33 kV project cutting network losses from about 16 per cent to 6 per cent, and renewables at 4.2 per cent of supply against 20 MWp of installed capacity
note: no outage-duration or interruption-frequency series is published, so reliability is described by coverage and losses rather than measured by downtime

subject: infra.energy
name: Renewable Energy Acceleration Program (World Bank P505856)
milestone: Project effective 26 February 2026
position_end: The programme became effective on 26 February 2026 with the utility advancing procurement. Its targets — 18 MW of renewable capacity, 18 MWh of storage enabled, a 7 per cent average reduction in outage duration and 500 grid-connected businesses benefiting by May 2030 — all stood at zero at 28 February 2026

subject: infra.capacity
name: Electronic Government Network (DICT)
milestone: Assembly committee visit, June 2025
position_end: The department's Network Operations Section administers and expands the Electronic Government Network, the national infrastructure district administrations and other ministries and agencies connect to; the department was described as running the network and the SeyID platform with 74 staff
note: no separately branded local-government ICT programme was found; this is the general infrastructure the question rests on

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Budapest Convention on Cybercrime accession
milestone: National Assembly unanimously approved accession motion, tabled by Hon. Sylvanne Lemiel
position_end: Assembly vote passed unanimously; the accession itself, an executive act, still to follow
note: Body of the source is paywalled beyond the lede

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Baseline
milestone: Introduced at a banking-sector workshop, October 2025
position_end: The National Cybersecurity Coordination Committee introduced a National Cybersecurity Baseline at a joint workshop with the bankers' association, with a member bank presenting a case study
note: the baseline document itself is not published, so what is held is its announcement

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Coordination Committee
milestone: Ran a World Press Freedom Day workshop with AMPS on AI's impact on press freedom, ethics and cybersecurity
position_end: Active as national cyber-coordination body; one documented activity
note: No founding instrument or mandate document held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy 2019-2024
milestone: Adopted for 2019-2024; no successor on record
position_end: The department's own founding strategy sets the CERT-SC and Cybersecurity Unit governance structure, mandatory information-security auditing of ministries, departments and agencies, and a 2019-2024 action plan for protecting government ICT infrastructure. Its period has expired and no successor is held
note: no audit result, incident figure or evaluation against the action plan is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Seychelles–AfCFTA–Quest Ghana digital-trade-hub MoU
status: Under review, established but terms unheld
milestone: Corridor joint venture signed with Ghana 2026-08-31
position_end: the continental secretariat signing a joint venture in Accra with the same technology company to establish the digital trade corridor, while the Seychelles memorandum remains under review
note: The Digital Trade Corridor HQ in Victoria claim is not established — do not conflate with the MoU itself

subject: dpi.id
name: CertExpress (online civil-status certificates)
milestone: Announced alongside the SeyID two-tier change; birth/marriage/death certificates online, 2-working-day delivery, saved to the SeyID E-Doc wallet
position_start: Live, SCR 50 fee (as stated at launch)
position_end: Unchanged; fee not re-verified since 2024-09
sources: 2024-09-18 Launch of New Digital Solutions for Public Services

subject: dpi.id
name: SeyID national digital-identity platform
milestone: Minor ID and digital driving licence added to the ID-Wallet, 2026
position_start: Two-tier structure already in place (2025-08): virtual-only for new work-permit holders since 17 Sep 2024, physical option retained for citizens
position_end: The platform authenticates with a password and second factor through its own authenticator app, a digital certificate or email, built on OpenID Connect and a commercial PKI. Its ID-Wallet now carries a Virtual ID Card built with Immigration and Civil Status and a Digital Driving Licence connected live to the licensing authority's own system, and a parent-activated Minor ID presenting a child's virtual card by QR code against an existing national identity number. Outside its own domain the credential gates the licensing authority's business and vehicle services on monServis, and the social protection platform launched in October 2025
sources: 2026-01-01-seyid-idwallet|2026-01-01-seyid-security|2026-01-01-seyid-minor-id-wallet|2023-04-19-sla-online-services-seyid-monservis|2025-10-21-asp-connect-digital-system-launch|2024-09-18 Launch of New Digital Solutions for Public Services|2024-09-18 Seychelles Makes Digital ID Mandatory for Work Permit Holders|2022-11-01 Seychelles Civil Status Act Cap 34 (as at 1 Nov 2022)
note: the credential rests on administrative practice rather than a statute of its own, and no enrolment, active-user or authentication-volume figure is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cheque phase-out (Central Bank of Seychelles, four-stage schedule)
milestone: CBS announced four dated stages: stop issuing to individuals 1 Jan 2025, stop accepting from individuals 1 May 2025, stop issuing to non-residents 1 Jan 2026, stop accepting from non-residents after 1 May 2026
position_start: Individual-facing stages running; non-resident stages not yet reached (2025-08)
position_end: SRC introduced cheque thresholds for tax/duties (eff. 13 Jul 2026) as part of a plan to discontinue cheques entirely by 31 Dec 2028
sources: 2024-09-22 Seychelles to phase out cheques for financial transactions from 2025|2026-07-09-nation-src-cheque-phaseout-2028
note: The ~600,000-cheques-in-2023 and >10m card/SEFT figures carry a date_source: proxy caveat

subject: dpi.pay
name: Financial consumer protection in payments
milestone: Statutory regime since 2022; first held enforcement 2026
position_start: A statute with no enforcement on record
position_end: The Financial Consumer Protection Act 2022 covers payment service providers and the operators of payment, clearing and settlement systems, and the December 2025 amendment to the payment licensing regulations makes safe and reliable IT systems a condition of licence. The clearest consumer-facing action the base holds is the 2026 warning that an unlicensed exchange operator left users without any route to recovery
note: no complaints statistic, ombudsman route or redress figure under the 2022 Act is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Foreign Exchange Act 2009 amendment (authorised-dealer perimeter)
milestone: Cabinet approved amendments widening authorised dealer to include credit unions and licensed payment service providers
position_end: Cabinet approval only; no Bill text, commencement date or transitional provision on record

subject: dpi.pay
name: Fusepay (B2B fintech, virtual business accounts)
milestone: First live transaction on Fusepay's Seychelles payments platform
position_end: Live payments platform plus a July-2026 Fuse360 AI-operations layer; Seychelles live, Mauritius scheduled Sep 2026
note: Pre-seed financing article held twice under two slugs — see byproducts note

subject: dpi.pay
name: ISO 20022 payment messaging migration
milestone: Adoption date set for 22 November 2025
position_end: The central bank and the bankers’ association jointly notified adoption of the ISO 20022 messaging standard for all domestic and cross-border electronic payments, replacing SWIFT MT formats, with effect from 22 November 2025
note: no completion statement or migration report after the effective date is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Payment System (Electronic Money) Regulations 2022 (S.I. 128 of 2022)
milestone: Made by the Central Bank under s.42(1) of the National Payment System Act 2014; incumbents had 6 months to comply, 1 year to reach the capital floor
position_end: Unchanged
note: Acquired from the Official Gazette only on 2026-08-03 — a foundational text newly added to the base, not a new development

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment service provider licensing
milestone: First held provider licence approved 14 November 2025
position_start: No licensed non-bank provider on record
position_end: The central bank granted a payment service provider licence enabling digital money accounts, instant and invoice payments and a cheque product, with a first live transaction reported five days later
note: the announcement is the licensee’s own; the central bank publishes no register of licensed payment institutions

subject: dpi.pay
name: Population uptake of financial services
milestone: Most recent national survey 2016
position_start: 94 per cent of adults banked in 2016
position_end: The most recent Seychelles-specific adult financial-inclusion survey, from 2016, found 94 per cent of adults banked, the highest rate in the region at the time. The central bank’s 2025 annual report is the newest official release covering payment-system activity
note: no population-level digital-payment or mobile-money uptake survey since 2016 is held, so a decade-old banking rate is the only national figure

subject: dpi.pay
name: UPI — Unified Payments Interface (India, NPCI MoU)
milestone: NPCI International and the Central Bank of Seychelles signed an MoU during PM Modi's visit; rollout targeted end-2026
position_end: MoU signed, regulatory prep under way (standards, cybersecurity, interoperability, merchant training); not yet delivered
note: Secondary source; CBS/NPCI primary not held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Virtual asset service provider regime
milestone: Enforcement action against an unlicensed operator, 26 May 2026
position_start: A licensing regime newly in force with unlicensed operators trading
position_end: The regulator consulted industry on the licensing framework in early 2024, recording about fifteen written responses and fifty to sixty live participants. From 1 January 2025 it named more than twenty entities that had not filed for transition as operating illegally, stated in May 2025 that one of them had been dissolved in 2024 without ever holding or applying for a licence, and in May 2026 identified its operator as unlicensed under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act 2024, warning publicly that it could neither investigate nor help recover users’ funds
note: no count of licences granted or refused under the 2024 Act is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land Register and its digitalisation
milestone: Land search system announced as coming soon, 2026
position_start: A paper register under the 1967 Act
position_end: The Land Registration Act of 1967, consolidated to 30 June 2014 and still the operative framework, establishes the Land Registry, the Land Register and the office of Land Registrar and governs registration, dispositions, searches and fees. The lands department and the ICT department tendered in November 2024 for a Land Management Administration Information System interfacing with the National Population Database, SeyID, Immigration and the Registration Division, on a nine-month delivery from award, and the Registration Division announced a new land search system as coming soon in 2026
note: no award, commissioning or completion statement for the information system is held, and the search system is announced rather than launched

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Addressing and Postcode System (S42 standard)
milestone: Cabinet approved the National Addressing System Bill, 3 April 2026
position_end: Cabinet approved the Seychelles National Addressing System Bill 2026, establishing a National Addressing Department and a National Addressing Database Unit — a new national reference-data layer the Vice-President describes as improving cross-agency access to data, short of an interoperability platform itself
sources: 2026-04-03-seychelles-national-addressing-system-bill-cabinet|2025-01-01 National Addressing System - Seychelles Postal Regulator
note: Source is undated (proxy-dated to 2025); status may have moved since capture, nothing later on record

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Population Database
milestone: Statutory custody with the Civil Status Division
position_end: The Civil Status Division has custody of the National Population Database and prepares and issues identity cards to all residents under the Civil Status Act and the Identity Card Act. The statistics bureau draws its population releases from those civil-status and immigration records: an all-resident population of 122,730 at 30 June 2025 and 123,097 at 31 December 2025
note: no coverage or completeness estimate for the database itself is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Register of Voters
milestone: The 2026 register certified 31 March 2026
position_end: The provisional 2026 register went out for inspection between 27 January and 13 February 2026 under section 8(1) of the Elections Act, and the chief registration officer certified the 2026 register on 31 March 2026, with certified copies distributed to eight political parties. The Commission's own 2025 report records 73,627 voters certified in March 2025, the register reopened on 14 October 2025 for 1,597 post-election transactions to the end of the year, and an online registration portal and tablet-based voter tagging deployed for the 2025 elections
note: the 2026 certified total is not stated in what is held, so only the 2025 figure can be given

subject: dpi.registry
name: Registrar General's Office digitalisation (business registration & IP)
milestone: President Ramkalawan toured the Registrar General's Office, praised digitalisation, announced unspecified legislative reforms
position_start: Digitalisation praised, unspecified reform commitment (2025-08, already the position)
position_end: Unchanged — no named bill, no date, nothing later on record
sources: 2025-02-10 Seychelles Pledges to Modernize Public Services Through Digital Transformation

subject: dpi.registry
name: Social assistance register and the Electronic Social Protection System
milestone: Cabinet stabilisation arrangement, 4 March 2026
position_start: A statutory duty with no platform behind it
position_end: The Agency for Social Protection Act 2011 requires the agency, at section 5(e), to maintain a national database of every applicant for and beneficiary of social assistance. The Electronic Social Protection System announced in December 2024 for a third-quarter 2025 go-live launched internally on 15 October 2025 as ASP Connect, reached through the SeyID portal; in March 2026 Cabinet extended its vendor support through 2026 and directed the ICT department to lead the transition to full government ownership and a long-term national platform
note: the lender's June 2025 status report records inter-agency information-sharing protocols signed with health, employment and education while the management information system behind the social registry remained pending

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register and business registration
milestone: Digital acknowledgment notice from 1 April 2026
position_end: The Revenue Administration (Business Registration and Declaration of Operation) Regulations 2022, in force from 1 January 2023, govern registration with the revenue commission, the issuing of tax identification numbers and active, suspended, dormant and deregistered taxpayer status. From 1 April 2026 taxpayers receive a digital acknowledgment notice on lodgement in place of a paper assessment letter, under regulations of November 2025 giving electronic filing its legal basis
note: no count of registered taxpayers or of returns filed electronically is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: ASYCUDA World customs system
milestone: Upgraded to version 4.4.1, 13-14 March 2026
position_end: The customs system was upgraded to version 4.4.1 over 13 and 14 March 2026, adding self-assessment and paperless bill-of-entry processing and pushing pre-payment, electronic payment and bank transfer ahead of cash and cheque. An ePayment facility for customs duties, built on the same system and delivered under the economic partnership agreement with the European Union, had launched in June 2024
note: no declaration volume, clearance time or electronic-payment share is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: e-Sanjeevani / e-Office / e-Hospital (India DPI platforms)
milestone: Firstpost reports bilateral consultations advancing between India and Seychelles toward potential adoption
position_end: Consultations advancing as reported 2026-08-08; no MoU, pilot or date established
note: Single secondary analytical source, no Seychelles-side primary

subject: dpi.mis
name: Electronic Health Information System
milestone: Digital health made a pillar of the July 2026 reform programme
position_end: The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 records that data capture is primarily paper-based, that implementation of an electronic health information system begun in 2020 had stalled, and that no formal data-governance standards existed; the ministry's own 2022 annual report puts the start in late 2021 with slow progress. The July 2026 reform programme makes digital health and data-driven decisions one of seven strategic pillars, and in February 2026 the President discussed real-time patient-data systems with an Indian hospital group ahead of a March technical visit
note: the repeal of the Health Care Agency in 2026 folds its functions and records into the ministry, removing an institutional boundary around health-information governance without specifying any technical interoperability

subject: dpi.mis
name: Huawei/CWS SMART Education
milestone: Ministry of Education, CWS and Huawei launched SMART Education (multimedia lessons, real-time assessment, IdeaHub) across four secondary schools
position_start: Did not exist immediately before Aug 2025
position_end: Live in four schools; no scale-up reported since
note: Vendor case study, not verified against a ministry primary

subject: dpi.mis
name: OpenEMIS education management information system
milestone: National go-live, March 2026
position_end: The education ministry took its new national education management information system live in March 2026, announced by the implementation partner
note: the announcement is the implementing partner’s; no ministry statement, school-coverage figure or interoperability specification is held

subject: dpi.mis
name: Police case-management system
milestone: Digital dispatch consoles handed over, 8 May 2026
position_start: A bespoke case-management application across police stations
position_end: A bespoke case-management application, built by a local integrator with United Nations support on a commercial low-code platform, is deployed across police stations with cross-district search. In May 2026 the disaster-management department and the police signed a memorandum of agreement covering handheld radios, base-station repeaters, solar equipment and digital dispatch consoles for emergency coordination
note: the case-management system is described by its vendor rather than by the police or government, and no station count or case volume is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Ease of Doing Business one-stop portal
milestone: Build contract awarded December 2025; government service centre approved May 2026
position_end: The tender board recorded the award of the supply and implementation of the Ease of Doing Business Portal to a Norwegian registers developer at USD 1,295,452.86, with a separate project-manager engagement; Cabinet approved a linked Government Service Centre in May 2026
note: Vendor press release, not verified against a ministry primary

subject: dpi.govtech
name: egov.sc government portal
milestone: VP/ICT Minister Pillay relaunched egov.sc, coinciding with the 50th Independence anniversary
position_end: Relaunched portal, single-click access framing

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic Case Management System (justice sector)
milestone: President Herminie officially launched ECMS, live with immediate effect
position_end: Operational online platform for the AG's Office/legal sector — shared calendars, virtual meetings, case-data retrieval, secure chat; financed by the US State Department via UNODC's Global Maritime Crime Programme and UNOPS

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic Certificate of Origin (e-CO)
milestone: Seychelles Revenue Commission, with the COMESA Secretariat, launched the e-CO for trade facilitation
position_end: Live; traders urged to use it to claim reduced duties under trade agreements

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Mandatory e-invoicing system (Seychelles Revenue Commission)
milestone: Acting Commissioner General Fred Morel: EOI opened March 2026, procurement now at final stage
position_end: Final-stage procurement; no award, vendor, go-live date or transaction threshold on record

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Revenue commission digitalisation programme
milestone: Digital acknowledgment notice from 1 April 2026
position_start: Customs paid over the counter, returns filed on paper
position_end: Customs duties have been payable online since June 2024, electronic filing of tax documents gained its legal basis in November 2025, and from April 2026 a digital acknowledgment notice replaces the paper assessment letter. From April 2026 Cabinet also required electronic or bank-transfer payment of customs dues of R50,000 and above and operationalised the ATA Carnet system

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Social protection delivery platform
milestone: Stakeholders briefed 2026-08-18
position_end: A digital platform for social-protection service delivery whose development began in 2022 on a multilateral recommendation, presented to government agencies, business partners and corporate beneficiaries at a stakeholder meeting
note: briefed rather than launched; no go-live date, beneficiary count or service list is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Video-enforcement pilot (automated traffic ticketing, Roche Caiman)
milestone: VP Afif announced an eight-week pilot repurposing the public CCTV estate for automated offence detection and remote e-tickets; partner Acusensus (Australia)
position_end: Eight-week pilot at Roche Caiman, Mahe; permanent adoption to depend on results
note: No data-protection basis stated on record

subject: digital.localgov
name: Digitisation of district-administration systems
position_end: Not held
note: No source on file

subject: digital.rural
name: Dedicated rural digital-service programme
position_end: Not held
note: No source on file distinct from the outer-island Starlink entry

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI in Education Framework 2026–2030
milestone: Cabinet approved the 21-page policy; covers every state school, AI literacy across the curriculum, mandatory AI micro-credential for teachers, an AI Champion per school, a Steering Committee maintaining approved/prohibited AI tool lists
position_end: Cabinet-approved, running to 2030; two World Bank pilots already running; the Framework's own text is not held
note: Implementation timeline, budget, indicators and tool-approval criteria unestablished; one automated acquisition attempt (2026-08-09) failed to locate the document

subject: tech.industry
name: Information and communication sector in the national accounts
milestone: National accounts bulletin for 2024
position_end: Information and communication is identified as a distinct economic activity contributing 0.4 percentage points to real GDP growth of 3.4 per cent in 2024
note: the bulletin does not disaggregate software, hardware or exports, so the figure establishes an operating sector and not its shape

subject: tech.innovate
name: Business, Technology and Innovation Incubator
milestone: Applications opened for the 2026 cohort, August 2026
position_end: A conservation trust launched the incubator with support from the science and innovation institute and two environmental funds, opening applications for a 2026 cohort offering up to twelve months of incubation, mentoring and access to seed funding
note: the announcement is the implementing trust’s own; no cohort size or fund size is stated

subject: tech.innovate
name: COMFWB Seychelles Incubation and Innovation Hub
milestone: Groundbreaking at Ile Perseverance, 21 July 2026
position_end: Ground was broken at Ile Perseverance on a hub under a COMESA, AUDA-NEPAD and COMFWB partnership, to house equipment procured under European technical assistance, with construction and operation expected in 2027
note: a committed project rather than an operating hub; no budget figure is stated

subject: tech.innovate
name: Seed Capital Grant Scheme
milestone: Policy revisions approved by Cabinet, 13 May 2026
position_end: Cabinet approved revisions to the scheme: a clearer definition of a youth beneficiary, revised eligibility, safeguards against repeat applicants, more flexible evaluation and extended implementation periods
note: no grant count, disbursement total or survival rate of funded ventures is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: UniSey Centre for Innovation
milestone: Established 2025 under the Faculty of Research and Innovation
position_end: An incubator and accelerator connecting students, researchers, entrepreneurs and industry, and the clearest currently operating technology hub the base holds
note: no cohort size, tenant list or funding figure is published

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Civil-service digital capacity building (India NCGG programme)
milestone: First cohort graduated 22 May 2026
position_end: A memorandum between India’s National Centre for Good Governance and the Public Service Bureau, exchanged during the February 2026 state visit, commits to training 250 Seychellois civil servants over three years. The first cohort of 29 officials — from information technology, the judiciary, education and other senior posts — began on 11 May 2026 and completed a two-week programme covering digital public infrastructure, electronic courts and AI-enabled governance on 22 May
note: no assessment, certification rate or measure of digital skill in the civil service is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Accredited computing and information-systems qualifications
milestone: Accreditation register of October 2023; new data short course July 2026
position_start: Two accredited computing programmes, one lapsing
position_end: The qualifications authority's programme register records the university's Diploma in Computing and IT accredited from February 2022 to February 2027, and the technology institute's National Diploma in Information Systems Engineering accredited from September 2019 to September 2024 and not shown renewed. Two additions have since been made outside the degree structure: a revenue commission agreement in April 2026 creating internships and an employment pathway for computing and information-systems students, and a data governance, analysis and privacy short course run with Oxford for public-sector staff in July 2026
note: no enrolment or completion figure for any of the programmes is published

subject: capacity.training
name: AI Student Tutor Programme (World Bank pilot)
milestone: Personalised AI learning support for Secondary 3 Maths and Geography
position_end: Piloting across four schools
note: Exact pilot-start date not given

subject: capacity.training
name: AI Teacher Coach Programme (World Bank pilot)
milestone: World Bank/Ministry of Education pilot: AI-assisted lesson-planning and classroom-practice guidance for Primary 5-6 teachers
position_end: Piloting across six schools; to become integral to the national Framework as implementation proceeds
note: Exact pilot-start date not given

subject: capacity.training
name: Graduate employment target and outcomes
milestone: University strategic plan 2022-2030
position_end: The university sets a target that every graduate across all programmes be employed within six months of completion, log-framed to 2030, and lists computing, artificial intelligence and data-science skilling among market opportunities. The April 2026 revenue-commission agreement creates an internship and possible employment pathway for computing students
note: no ICT-specific graduate-outcome figure is published in any document held

subject: include.access
name: National accessibility framework
milestone: Absence stated by the Office of the First Lady, May 2026
position_end: Concrete accessibility retrofits are recorded at the Office of the First Lady and a stadium ramp, and the same statement identifies the absence of a National Accessibility Action Plan and a supporting legislative framework as the structural gap, with a presidential pledge to legislate. The 2025 voluntary national review states that social protection is being digitised to reach the elderly and people with disabilities
note: the absence is stated by the government itself rather than inferred from silence

subject: include.access
name: National Gender Policy and girls in technology
milestone: Policy adopted January 2012
position_start: A 2012 policy with no dated activity behind it
position_end: The 2012 National Gender Policy requires gender mainstreaming across policy, including the promotion of women’s access to information and communication technology. In August 2026 Seychelles joined a girls-in-space programme training participants in satellite, CubeSat and geospatial data skills, referencing a science, technology and innovation department established in the education ministry earlier the same year
note: no sex-disaggregated figure for internet use, ICT employment or computing enrolment is held

subject: include.access
name: Public support for access to government information
milestone: Afrobarometer round fielded 2025, dispatch published 2026-08-11
position_end: 62% say the public should have access to government information against 25% who say it is for officials only; 84% want district-administration budgets published and 82% want information on bids and contracts, while 47% would publish the salaries of district administrators and teachers

subject: include.access
name: Refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced people
milestone: UNHCR submission to the 38th Universal Periodic Review session
position_end: The refugee agency’s own submission states there are no known refugees or asylum seekers, no known cases of statelessness and no known internally displaced people in Seychelles
note: a dated statement that the population does not exist, not an undocumented gap; Seychelles has not ratified the 1951 Convention

subject: include.divides
name: Universal access and universal service regime
milestone: Established by Part XII of the Communications Act 2023
position_end: Sections 97 to 102 of the Communications Act 2023 establish universal access and universal service policy, obligations and a fund, administered by the communications regulator. Against that, a commercial tracker puts 87.4 per cent of the population online at October 2025, leaving an estimated 16,800 people, 12.6 per cent, offline
note: no disbursement from the fund, designated provider obligation or coverage target set under it is held, three years after the Act

subject: data.statistics
name: Censuses and national surveys
milestone: Second economic-activities census pilot, April 2026
position_start: The 2022 census reported, no business census
position_end: The 2022 Population and Housing Census — the sixth since independence and the first conducted digitally, under the Census Act — was reported in March 2024. A new Census of Economic Activities entered a first pilot in November 2025 and a second in April 2026, ahead of a main round scheduled for 2026 and 2027
note: the census report held is the preface and contents of a 233-page document; its statistical annexes were not captured

subject: data.statistics
name: Donor data-transformation programme
milestone: 2025 annual report published, framed on data-powered transformation
position_start: Did not exist as a reported programme
position_end: The country office’s 2025 annual report frames its work as data-powered transformation; the base holds an excerpt of the report rather than a programme document, so no budget, counterpart or deliverable is established

subject: data.statistics
name: Island states resilience data programme
milestone: National implementation launched 2026-08-18
position_end: National implementation launched of a nine-country African island-states programme backed by a US$4.943 million readiness grant, whose data leg is a standardised approach to institutional readiness, multi-hazard risk assessment and information systems for building pipelines of climate-resilient projects
note: the grant figure covers the nine-country programme, not the national share, which is not published

subject: data.statistics
name: National Strategy for the Development of Statistics 2023-2027
milestone: Mid-term evaluation mission held 16-20 February 2026
position_start: The first such strategy, newly adopted
position_end: The African Union peer review of May 2025 records adoption of the first national strategy for the development of statistics, aligned to Vision 2033 and Agenda 2063, notes the statistics bureau’s professional independence and recommends a new Statistics Bill. A mid-term evaluation mission ran from 16 to 20 February 2026, and in June 2026 the bureau completed an externally funded review of its organisational structure recommending it strengthen its role coordinating the national statistical system
note: the evaluation’s findings and the review’s report are not themselves published

subject: data.open
name: Fisheries Information Management System
milestone: Showcased to a visiting delegation, June 2026
position_end: The responsible ministry describes an operating Fisheries Information Management System giving public access to fisheries statistics, licensing and export data — the clearest operating open-data system the base holds for Seychelles. An openly licensed national energy-system dataset covering demand, cost, efficiency and emissions parameters to 2050 was published in May 2026
note: no dataset count, download figure or licensing statement for the system is published

subject: data.open
name: Open government data policy
milestone: A corrective action set in 2020 and not shown closed
position_end: The extractives transparency board found in September 2020 that revenue data was published in open format but that the multi-stakeholder group did not appear to have an open data policy, and set a corrective-action deadline to publish one. Nothing held records that policy. In December 2025 the statistics bureau opened two externally financed expressions of interest to modernise its website and improve public access to national data — a procurement step, not a portal
note: a dated, cited absence: the corrective action names the missing instrument and nothing since records it being made

subject: data.satellite
name: Earth-observation data for agriculture and land
milestone: Vegetation-index dataset updated to 28 February 2026
position_start: A regional readiness ranking with no national product
position_end: A humanitarian data platform publishes a Seychelles subnational vegetation-index dataset derived from satellite imagery, updated on 3 March 2026 with ten-day values through 28 February 2026. Terms of reference issued on 11 March 2026 seek a national consultancy to analyse Landsat and Sentinel imagery of land productivity and land cover for desertification reporting. A regional benchmark had earlier placed Seychelles third of sixteen states on digital agriculture readiness
note: the vegetation product is produced outside Seychelles; no national Earth-observation capability or ground-truthing programme is held

subject: data.satellite
name: UN COPUOS accession / UNOOSA engagement
milestone: Cabinet approved accession to the UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space and engagement with UNOOSA, framed as building geospatial-data capability for maritime security, disaster preparedness, ocean management
position_end: Cabinet approval only; accession process and any programme not yet on record

subject: geopol.usa
name: United States bilateral engagement
milestone: Maritime law-enforcement agreement signed and in force 27 July 2021
position_end: The clearest signed bilateral instrument the base holds is the counter-illicit maritime activity, or shiprider, agreement of 27 July 2021, whose 21 articles cover boarding, jurisdiction, overflight and the use of force. It is law enforcement rather than digital cooperation
note: no United States hyperscaler, cloud or digital-infrastructure commitment to Seychelles is held

subject: geopol.china
name: Huawei vendor relationship (5G core + SMART Education)
milestone: CWS launched 5G with Huawei (2020); Ministry of Education, CWS and Huawei launched SMART Education across four schools (2025-08)
position_start: Huawei already CWS's 5G vendor; SMART Education just beginning (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged — Huawei remains CWS's core vendor; no reported scale-up of SMART Education beyond the four pilot schools
note: China's Hytera also holds the stalled emergency-comms MoU with CWS

subject: geopol.eu
name: European Union digital cooperation with Seychelles
status: Implemented, cooperation agreed rather than delivered
milestone: Enhanced Economic Partnership Agreement negotiations concluded 10 June 2026
position_end: The ninth political dialogue of October 2022 recorded an agreement to explore cooperation on cybersecurity, disinformation, safer internet use and the protection of personal data. In June 2026 the Union and four eastern and southern African states including Seychelles concluded negotiations on an enhanced Economic Partnership Agreement carrying a binding prohibition of unjustified data-localisation requirements and a permanent ban on customs duties on electronic transmissions. The 2026-2030 fisheries protocol, published in the Official Journal in August 2026, sets confidentiality and personal-data rules for the electronic vessel data the parties exchange, and the data protection regulator met European justice and delegation officials on cooperation and capacity building in February 2026
note: no European digital project, grant or infrastructure investment in Seychelles is held; what the base carries is trade rules, fisheries data terms and regulator contact

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf-state engagement with Seychelles
status: Implemented, payments cooperation signed, no digital investment held
milestone: Two central-bank memoranda signed 19 July 2024
position_end: Two memoranda between the central banks of the United Arab Emirates and Seychelles, signed on 19 July 2024, cover settlement in local currencies and the interlinking of instant-payment platforms, electronic switches and messaging systems, and name financial technology and central bank digital currency as cooperation areas. In May 2026 the Emirates reaffirmed commitments to four desalination plants, a sports complex and housing, and opened preliminary talks on direct oil procurement; the education ministry separately partnered with the Emirati Digital School Programme in April 2026
note: two years after the payments memoranda, nothing records an interlinked switch, a live corridor or a digital-currency pilot between the two

subject: geopol.india
name: India bilateral engagement
milestone: Nine instruments signed on the state visit of 28 June 2026
position_start: A standing relationship with no in-window digital instrument
position_end: India’s own bilateral brief of August 2024 inventories agreements back to 1981, including a 2010 information-technology centre memorandum and a 2018 cybersecurity memorandum. The February 2026 state visit produced a joint vision in which India commits to comprehensive work on the build-out of Seychelles’ digital public infrastructure including digital payments, a Digital Transformation memorandum between the two ICT ministries, a civil-service capacity-building memorandum, and a USD 175 million special economic package covering e-mobility among other sectors. The June 2026 visit produced nine further instruments, among them a payments memorandum between India’s international payments company and the central bank and an umbrella line of credit of INR 1,250 crore
note: the memoranda are commitments; nothing yet records a delivered system, a disbursement or a live payments corridor under any of them
